actionable_steps.citation: Experience Divinity Within In Total Silence — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 37 (2004), 2004-11-22
actionable_steps.step: Resolve to be the master of your mind, not its slave — keep it steady and fixed on God through the day.

actionable_steps.citation: The jewel in the iron safe — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 15 (1981 - 82), 1982-11-20
actionable_steps.step: When the monkey-mind runs after pleasures, don't send the body along with it. Tell the mind plainly: I shall not give you the body as your servant.

actionable_steps.citation: Renunciation and Realisation — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 21 (1988), 1988-07-11
actionable_steps.step: Practise being indifferent to the mind's vagaries — that indifference is the real meaning of mind control.
Let your intellect interrogate every rising thought: is it good or bad, will it help or hinder, where will it lead?

actionable_steps.citation: Krishna thrishna — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 6 (1966)
actionable_steps.step: Fasten the monkey mind with the chain of devotion — transmute the desires that torment you into thirst for God.

definition.citation: Vinayaka - The Master Of Siddhi And Buddhi — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 34 (2001), 2001-08-22
definition.quote: Mind is given to enquire. Body is granted to perform. The Atma monitors the performance of these two. Atma is permanent. Mind is fickle and has to be made steady.

discourses.citation: Experience Divinity Within In Total Silence — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 37 (2004), 2004-11-22
discourses.quote: Make your mind steady and fix it on God. Mind is the cause of everything in this world. Mind by itself does not go anywhere. It is we who direct it and divert it in different ways according to our whims and fancies. We are responsible for its unsteadiness. … You should be the master of your mind and not its slave.

discourses.citation: The jewel in the iron safe — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 15 (1981 - 82), 1982-11-20
discourses.quote: Let the monkey run; you keep quiet where you are; do not let the body go along with the monkey-mind. Tell the mind, "I shall not give you the body as your servant." Then, the mind will desist and it can be defeated.

discourses.citation: Renunciation and Realisation — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 21 (1988), 1988-07-11
discourses.quote: Nigraham (control) really means being indifferent to the vagaries of the mind. … When it is realised that the mind is made up of thoughts and doubts, the elimination of the thoughts is the means of restraining the mind.

discourses.citation: Krishna thrishna — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 6 (1966)
discourses.quote: Devotion to Krishna is the chain by which the monkey mind can be fastened and subdued. Transmute all the desire with which the senses torment you into the thirst for Krishna and you are saved.

make_it_real: You can't stop the monkey from jumping — but you can stop handing it your body as its playground.
title: Mind Control

vahinis.quote: The mind can cause bondage, but it can also confer liberation. … The mind (manas) is but a bundle of thoughts, a complex of wants and wishes.
Uproot the impulses that make up the mind, and the mind is no more. … The mind is like a piece of cloth; it takes on any colour with which it is dyed.
